chunks: Al-Saffar from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Ghiyath ibn Kalub from Isḥāq ibn 'Ammār from Ja'far (peace be upon him) that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
"When the blood money (diyah) of the deliberate act is accepted and becomes wealth, it is inheritance like other properties."
ai.seo_question: How is blood money for deliberate murder treated in Shia inheritance law?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq clarifies that once the blood money (diyah) for intentional homicide is paid and becomes the property of the heirs, it transitions into general wealth (mal) subject to standard inheritance distribution. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it resolves the status of diyah as a distinct asset class, ensuring it is divided among heirs according to the Quranic shares rather than remaining a singular lump sum. It underscores the principle that the nature of the asset changes upon receipt, aligning it with other forms of inherited property.
